answer: In an agent garden, a newcomer can only join when three established agents co-sign its entry, each locking 50 tokens as collateral against its behaviour. If it cheats, the co-signers lose part of their stake, so they vet applicants carefully. A Sybil attacker must bribe three trusted agents for every fake identity, and each bribe must exceed what those agents risk losing — the cost echoes across every copy. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly, so cheap mass identities arrive too weak to matter.
